text: It's all very tricky. Turns out a lot of people in the world genuinely intend for good outcomes and accept different trade-offs on a lot of axes, and use power to achieve outcomes that reflect their trade-off preferences, resulting in a mix of good and bad that's hard to judge.

author: jachiam0
text: As an individual, when trying to honestly evaluate other individuals, you have to very carefully disentangle the stories and facts to figure out under what contexts people had what power and whether they used it responsibly, and/or in accordance with their real principles

author: jachiam0
text: Narratives around people's goodness or badness, or ability to contribute to discussion, often rely on figuring out what level of power they have, but usually context is stripped out to meet the needs of the narrative

author: jachiam0
text: It's difficult to effect system-level change without exerting power in a way that causes harm or discomfort for some, and this is a challenge for well-meaning people who want systems to change, especially when they care about harm reduction

author: jachiam0
text: Whenever you exert power you potentially cause an outcome contrary to other people's preferences, usually (but not always) creating some amount of harm and discomfort

author: jachiam0
text: You can expend power by moving current through a wire, and the power given off will be proportional to voltage times current (I promise this is the only lame joke tweet in this thread)

author: jachiam0
text: Attempting to cultivate, maintain, or use power can create circumstances where others have stupendous power over you - think of many politicians only allow themselves to say what their audience is open to hearing

author: jachiam0
text: Your experience of material circumstances - whether because they're too good or very damaging - can make you unaware of power you can exert, or are exerting, in other settings

author: jachiam0
text: You can create power orthogonal to your resources, shared beliefs, and skills by charisma and excitement, but you can't sustain it if you can't ground it in reality somehow

author: jachiam0
text: You can create power orthogonal to your resources and punch way above your weight by being highly individually productive and making things people want access to

author: jachiam0
text: You can create power orthogonal to your resources and punch way above your weight by tapping into shared beliefs

author: jachiam0
text: (I suspect this is largely true of many moderately-known professionals who look high-status but lack super-wealth and consequently live a weirdly fragile existence, at the mercy of the audience's whims or a health incident)

author: jachiam0
text: You can have sufficient resources and standing/fame that you appear to have power at the system level but have no ability to meaningfully change what other people do or assure anything but your own material survival

author: jachiam0
text: You can have next-to-no power at the system level and have massive power in a much smaller setting

author: jachiam0
